manual_impact_questions: Which user-visible outcome and protected behavior can change?
Which callers, state/data owners, error paths, migrations, and relaunch outcomes are affected?
Which notification, Widget, Intent, Watch, window, background, or other platform consumers share this contract?
Does an existing Oracle fail on a credible wrong value/state, or must the change add or strengthen one?

minimum_evidence: quality selector unit/negative controls
Apple PR representative lane
escalation_reasons: Test infrastructure changes require one representative product journey; syntax alone is insufficient.

escalation_reasons: A changed UI Oracle must execute instead of being hidden behind a fixed curated scope list.

minimum_evidence: Swift message/search/deletion tests
iOS accurate content/search/delete/relaunch UI journeys
iOS provider refresh new-result/failure-recovery UI journeys
known_evidence_gaps: representative iOS/macOS local-cached media decode/click/preview, pagination/read, and slow, new-result, and failure-recovery refresh workflows are protected; multi-image, animation, share, cache eviction, and media performance remain incomplete.

minimum_evidence: iOS and macOS failed search must not masquerade as empty or stale results; Retry reaches one exact canonical result and matching detail
known_evidence_gaps: This focused recovery path does not claim index-rebuild integrity, 10k/100k search latency, physical-device behavior, or every query-normalization permutation.
escalation_reasons: Search presentation and query-owner changes can otherwise ship a plausible empty or stale list while the user cannot recover to the requested canonical message.

minimum_evidence: a real deletion immediately suppresses only its target
Undo restores the exact canonical object
deadline commit and relaunch keep the target absent while an unrelated message remains readable
known_evidence_gaps: This representative lifecycle does not claim multiple pending deletions, process death during claim, remote deletion conflicts, or backoff behavior.
escalation_reasons: Deletion ownership is irreversible after its deadline and must protect both restoration and durable commit, not merely the visible undo bar.

minimum_evidence: projection semantics tests including out-of-order head rejection

known_evidence_gaps: Event close slow/error/duplicate-submit recovery is protected on iOS and macOS. Precise single-Thing delete/control-object/relaunch is protected; deep links, bulk/channel deletion, and tombstones remain incomplete.
escalation_reasons: Entity projection/state owners feed list, detail, Thing relations, notifications, and system surfaces.

minimum_evidence: Apple PR broad positive representative set including Event close/filter/relaunch and Thing accurate search/single-delete/control-object/three-relation/relaunch
known_evidence_gaps: Pure screen composition changes do not automatically run fault injection, deep-link, bulk-delete, or tombstone matrices; run the owning focused risk path when the diff actually changes one of those contracts.
escalation_reasons: Pure presentation and stable action-entry changes need real positive UI outcomes, but should not automatically consume every Entity failure-recovery scenario.
